t: You're on Chesham Place, a street in Belgravia running between Belgrave Square and Pont Street. Today it is home to several embassies. It has had many distinguished residents. Irene Astor, who became Baroness Astor of Hever, was born here. She was a philanthropist who chaired the Sunshine Fund for Blind Children for over forty years and raised more than fourteen million pounds. Violet Douglas-Pennant was born here too, with her sisters Kathleen and Alice. Violet became the second commandant of the Women's Royal Air Force. Edward Beddington-Behrens, a patron of the arts and advocate of European co-operation, died here, as did the Earl of Courtown.
